# Doc 43 rule 2.3 #15: the source paths each nightly-, weekly- or dispatch-tier job of
# .github/workflows/ci.yml exercises, so a pull request that touches one knows which
# jobs to dispatch (`gh workflow run CI --ref <branch>`) and get green before it is
# marked ready. Pull-request CI never runs these jobs; the nightly of 2026-11-05 broke
# on #475, whose grace windows moved the M7 and M8 stories' pins.
#
# One line a path: `<job id> <tier> <path>`. The job id is the key under `jobs:` in
# ci.yml; the tier is `nightly` (the daily schedule), `weekly` (the Sunday 04:17
# schedule) or `dispatch` (by hand only), and must match the job's `if:`; the path
# is a workspace-relative file, or a directory prefix ending in `/`. A PR's changed
# file matches a line when it equals the path or starts with the prefix.
# scripts/nightly_advice.py prints the matches (the `lint` cell runs it on every pull
# request, and it runs locally the same way); `ci_policy::nightly_paths` refuses a
# job id ci.yml does not have, a non-PR job with no line, a wrong tier, and a path
# that does not exist.
#
# The stories run most of the engine, so the map is deliberately the paths a story's
# PINS move with: the timers, grace windows and terminal capacity (mush-core's
# action_state), the economy and market a story buys through, the minds and the
# registry, and each job's own test modules. Widen a line when a nightly breaks on a
# path it did not name, in the PR that fixes the nightly.

# M7: the genuine Registry ratings, the paid purchase and the player market stories.
mind-commerce-acceptance nightly crates/tacsim/src/minds/
mind-commerce-acceptance nightly crates/tacsim/src/hardware/flow/launch/
mind-commerce-acceptance nightly crates/mush-server/src/world_task/submission_disposition/
mind-commerce-acceptance nightly crates/mush-market/src/
mind-commerce-acceptance nightly crates/mush-economy/src/
mind-commerce-acceptance nightly crates/mush-core/src/action_state/
